answer: A harbor insurer hires agents to verify each vessel's voyage before paying a route-risk bounty. A summit weather station signs a forecast window, and the port signs one departure ID; the contract pays once per ID after independent arrival evidence matches the claim, no matter how many accounts submit it. A sybil operator must finance distinct real sailings and post a bond for each claim to earn more. Ports and crews could collude to invent trips, so random cargo audits and public route logs are needed, though storms can still hide honest evidence.
